TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
FRIDAY, 3 FEBRUARY 2023 AT 10:00 AM (AEST)
DAY 31
MR JUSTIN GREGGERY KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MR ANGUS SCOTT KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MS RENEE BERRY, Counsel Assisting
MS DOMINIQUE HOGAN-DORAN SC, for the Commonwealth
MR ALEXANDER VIAL, for the Commonwealth
MR GARETH BEACHAM KC, for Shane West

COMMISSIONER: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, thank you, Commissioner. I appear today with Ms Berry.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Ms Hogan-Doran?
MS HOGAN-DORAN: Commissioner, today I appear with Mr Vial for the Commonwealth.
COMMISSIONER: And Mr Beacham?
MR BEACHAM: Thank you, Commissioner. I appear for Mr West, instructed by King & Wood
Mallesons.
MR GREGGERY: Mr West is present.
COMMISSIONER: Mr West, will you take an oath or affirmation?
MR WEST: An affirmation.
<SHANE MICHAEL WEST, AFFIRMED
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Take a seat. Yes, Mr Greggery.
<EXAMINATION BY MR GREGGERY KC
MR GREGGERY: Mr West, can you tell the Commission your full name please?
MR WEST: Shane Michael West.
MR GREGGERY: And your occupation?
MR WEST: A partner at PricewaterhouseCoopers.
MR GREGGERY: You were served with a Notice to Give a Statement and Produce Documents,
NTG-0118, dated 18 November 2022, and have produced two Statements in response: The
first dated 1 December 2022, and the Supplementary Statement dated 6 December 2022.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. Commissioner, I tender the Exhibits on the draft list, numbered
3815 to 3980. That fills in the gap left last Friday.
COMMISSIONER: Yes. The Exhibits as numbered on the list from 3815 to 3980 are admitted.
Thank you.

MR GREGGERY: Broadly speaking, Mr West, the questions on the notice that was received by
you and your Supplementary Statements and the documents produced in addition to those
Statements deal with the engagement of PwC by the Department of Human Services in early
2017 in respect of what became known as the Robodebt Scheme. That's correct?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Before we get into the detail of the engagement and the work undertaken
by PwC, can you just give us a broad overview of how the engagement came about?
MR WEST: So it's my recollection that Kathryn Campbell made contact with one of our other
partners - a fellow partner to indicate that they might need some support in undertaking an
independent review and then that was forwarded to me and then, through conversations
with Jason McNamara and Kristen Foster at the time, an agreed Statement of Work was
entered into.
MR GREGGERY: PwC was familiar with the Department of Human Services before the initial
discussions that led to this particular scope of works?
MR WEST: Yes, we were.
MR GREGGERY: Had it had a long history of consulting or advising the Department in respect
of various matters?
MR WEST: Yes. Yes, like - without knowing the specifics of it, yes, we support a range of
government Departments and have done so for a number of years.
MR GREGGERY: And the support that you provide, to your experience, does it involve a level
of capability which the Department doesn't seem to possess itself?
MR WEST: Yes, it often does.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Although the initial engagement here was only a - I think an
engagement through to the 30 June 2017, there were a number of follow-on engagements
that ran for quite some time. That, indeed, lasted a number of years, I think?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: You identify in your Statement a number of stages or further phases of
projects which were carried out at least into 2020?
MR WEST: Yes, correct.
MR GREGGERY: If we turn to Exhibit 3819 - now we are just having - making some attempts,
Mr West, to identify which tab they might be in the hard copy bundle before you, because

screen. But if you would like to see the hard copy, we can make that happen. The partner of
yours who had initial contact with the Department was Mr Weber?
MR WEST: Yes, correct.
MR GREGGERY: The person identified there as the author of this email on 2 February 2017.
The Jason is, of course, Mr McNamara to whom you referred, and the Kathryn there is Ms
Campbell?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: The main liaison - point of liaison between PwC and the Department, did
that continue to be Ms Campbell or Mr McNamara?
MR WEST: Mr McNamara.
MR GREGGERY: And how regular was the contact between PwC and Mr McNamara?
MR WEST: During the course of the engagement or in the lead-up to?
MR GREGGERY: During the course of the engagement.
MR WEST: We would have met with Jason regularly, at least weekly.
MR GREGGERY: And - although you might generally be described - that is, PwC might
generally be described as an independent or external consultant, did the engagement
involve actually having PwC personnel on site at DHS?
MR WEST: Not this engagement, no.
MR GREGGERY: Subsequent engagements?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. After the initial contact was made by Mr Weber and Ms Campbell, I
take it you took over a more significant role in leading the revision of the scope of the
engagement?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: If we turn to Exhibit 3822 - we might start with 3821, sorry. During the
negotiations of around the scope of the engagement, you were dealing with Kristen Foster
from the Department?
MR WEST: Yes.

MR GREGGERY: And this email reflects part of the negotiations about the scope as at 8
February 2017?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And the way in which the negotiations over the scope were conducted was
the development of a Word document which was sent by you to Ms Foster, modified,
returned to you, modified, returned to her, until there was agreement reached.
MR WEST: Yes, that's right. I guess I'm not sure I categorise it as negotiations, but it
was - yes, that's how we sought to clarify what -
MR GREGGERY: Clarify the nature -
MR WEST: What the Department wanted, yes.
MR GREGGERY: The attachment referred to there is Exhibit 3822, which was brought up a
moment ago. And if the front page could be expanded, it might - some of the clarity seems to
be lost in the upload, but the editing of the document reflects the review between yourself
and Ms Foster about the scope of the works.
MR WEST: Yes, that's my recollection.
MR GREGGERY: At least at this stage, there was a description of fraud activities which had
been inserted, the removal of a reference to “policy” and, in respect of individual debt, the
removal of a reference to "recent high-profile" events from the background and some clarity
added around the Department requiring an independent review of the Customer Compliance
and fraud activities. Now, the ultimate landing point from the exchange between yourself
and Ms Foster was a document dated 13 February 2017, to your recollection?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct. Well, I think - so that's the ultimate landing of our proposal,
yes.
MR GREGGERY: Right.
MR WEST: I - the ultimate landing would be the work order that we subsequently signed.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Thank you. And if we can go to that document, it is Exhibit 1634, tab 17
in your hard copy bundle, Mr West. That's the final version of the proposal?
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And the proposal included PwC's proposed fees and expenses, and you can
see that on page .0009. And the official order that you referred to, which reflected the
agreement, that is the contractual agreement, is Exhibit 1635. Likely the following tab in
your bundle, Mr West.

COMMISSIONER: It's 19 in mine, if that's any help.
MR WEST: Yes, it's not next in the -
MR GREGGERY: And it confirms, Mr West, the date of 14 February as the date of the order;
the commencement date of the contract, 15 February 2017; completion date of 30 June
2017; and thereafter the objective and scope, the deliverables and the fees related to the
document - to the work, sorry. Now, can I take you, firstly, to the objective and scope,
paragraph 1.1. Was it communicated to you by Ms Foster or by Mr Weber, your partner, or
Mr McNamara, that the Department had not at any stage since the Budget Measure was
introduced in 2015, undertaken a type of review which is contemplated in this
subparagraph?
MR WEST: I don't recall ever being told that one hadn't taken place.
MR GREGGERY: Were you ever provided with any documents which indicated that
subparagraphs - the work in subparagraphs (a) to (e) had taken place at any point in time
within the Department prior to PwC's engagement?
MR WEST: My recollection is that we would have been provided with some process mapping
and business rules by the Department through the - undertaking this engagement. I'm not
sure when they were completed, though.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. To put it another way, was it your understanding, as the lead on the
project, that the work to be undertaken by PwC was really a complete review of the system
because that had not been done by the Department to this level?
MR WEST: It was my understanding that we have been asked to undertake this activity
because the - like, if I take the first one, the end-to-end processes as an example.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR WEST: There was a view that what the Department had documented at the time may not
have been 100 per cent accurate.
MR GREGGERY: Well, not only not 100 per cent accurate, but the task of undertaking an
end-to-end review had not been undertaken at all by the Department, I suggest.
MR WEST: I don't know.
MR GREGGERY: Is it that you don't know because you were never told that, or you don't
know because you were never given any documents indicating that?
MR WEST: Both of those.
MR GREGGERY: Both of those things.

MR WEST: Yes.
COMMISSIONER: When you say what the Department had documented may not have been
100 per cent accurate, what are you talking about?
MR WEST: The process maps in particular.
COMMISSIONER: And in what respects, do you recall? Were they thought -
MR WEST: I can recall conversations that - and it kind of speaks to the nature of the review
to not necessarily rely on things that had been documented to be provided to us, that they
wanted us to re-document, effectively.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you.
MR GREGGERY: That is, there was an indication to you or PwC that the documents which had
been generated by the Department ought not be - that there was a low degree of confidence
in their accuracy.
MR WEST: Yes, that there was the expectation that we shouldn't rely upon them in
undertaking our work.
MR GREGGERY: Right.
COMMISSIONER: Sounds like a level of mistrust in the work done to date.
MR WEST: Possibly, yes.
MR GREGGERY: If you go to paragraph 1.2, the heading Deliverables, it's subparagraphs (a)
through (d) over the next page. The first related to the delivery of business process maps,
documenting the current state of compliance and fraud activities. The second were process
maps documenting customer interaction with the Department's systems. And the third was a
report that identifies and analyses options for improvement and considers the
implementation of current Budget Measures. And the fourth was the development of a
high-level implementation plan or road map.
The third of those, is it the case that PwC produced or, rather, developed drafts of the report
referred to in subparagraph (c) throughout the life of this project, that is, towards June 2017,
but never finalised the drafts or the latest version of the draft?
MR WEST: Sort of. So we were developing a draft - we were developing a report through the
engagement.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.

MR WEST: It became clear at some point during the engagement that one of the documents
that we had provided to the client was considered the report for the purpose of that
deliverable. If that makes sense.
MR GREGGERY: Well, let's be clear about the document you had provided, which the
Department considered to be the report for paragraph 1.2(c). Was that a short-form
presentation?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: That is, a visual presentation, rather than a -
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: What might be traditionally understood as a report?
MR WEST: Yes. Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: That is, it wasn't the document that PwC was working on, the understanding
of the report.
MR WEST: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: It was a different version of a document? Now, the - there were interactions
between the Department and PwC in June 2017 which clarified the deliverables under the
contract. Have you seen some documents this morning about that?
MR WEST: I have, but they don't relate to that engagement. They relate to the deliverables
for the subsequent engagement.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. So just to be clear, Exhibit 4777 is a document - and email dated 19
June 2017. There is a reference there to May to June deliverables. That is not this - not the
works that we've been dealing with.
MR WEST: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: It's the next stage.
MR WEST: That's right. That's right.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Well, can we return, then, to the point at which PwC was advised
that the report identified in paragraph 1.2(c) of the deliverables was no longer required?
What's your recollection of that point?
MR WEST: So we provided a report. So it wasn't that a report was no longer required;
it's - we provided the report that - the presentation that you spoke of before was considered

MR GREGGERY: Maybe we are at cross-purposes. The draft report which was developed
during the period February to June 2017 is attached as - well, there are a number of versions
of it, but the latest one we will come to. Was - are you saying that the draft was considered
the report?
MR WEST: No, no, I'm saying that the - what you categorised as the presentation -
MR GREGGERY: The visual presentation.
MR WEST: - was considered the report.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR WEST: For the purpose of -
MR GREGGERY: For the purpose of that.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Which was obviously not PwC's understanding of the concept at the start of
the work.
MR WEST: Correct.
MR GREGGERY: Because PwC put considerable time and effort into developing what was
commonly understood as a written report which addressed the matters set out in the
proposal. And was then told that it was no longer required in that form.
MR WEST: No, so I don't think we were ever told - like, my recollection is that draft report
that you are referring to was never something seen by the Department or the client. It
was - so we were never told that that report was not required. We were told that what we
had previously provided them was considered the report for the purpose of the contract.
MR GREGGERY: Well, there must have been some discussion at some point about the fact
that PwC had developed a draft report.
MR WEST: So I think my recollection was our working - kind of our working understanding
going through that engagement was that we would be providing a report of that nature.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR WEST: So that's why we commenced the drafting of it. But prior to the completion of
even the drafting of it, it became clear that the previously provided presentation was - would
constitute the report for the purpose of the work order. So we saw no purpose in finalising
the thicker report.

MR GREGGERY: I can appreciate PwC's position. It wouldn't want to spend - invest any more
time or energy into finalising a document it was informed was not required. The point I'm
getting at is surely PwC communicated to the Department that it had, in fact, been
developing a report.
MR WEST: I can't recall ever communicating to the Department that we had - it was sort of
just - I guess it was our assumption that this went through the first couple of months of the
engagement that that was what the deliverable would look like, but at some point that
changed.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
COMMISSIONER: Well, you said it became clear that the presentation would constitute the
report. How did it become clear? Who said that?
MR WEST: I can't recall exactly who said it. But -
COMMISSIONER: It wasn't PwC's -
MR WEST: No, it wasn't. So it came - it would have come from the Department. If I was
speculating, it would have been Jason McNamara.
COMMISSIONER: See, this is actually a provision in your contractual arrangements, so it does
matter whether you meet your contractual obligations. Is there no record of how it comes
about that there's what looks rather like a variation of them?
MR WEST: So the - as I said, I -my recollection is that the Department was satisfied that - that
what we had previously given them was - constituted a report for the purpose of that
deliverable.
COMMISSIONER: Did you get them on record about that?
MR WEST: Not formally. But - other than they paid the invoice that was associated with the
deliverables.
COMMISSIONER: And you have no recollection of who you discussed it with?
MR WEST: Not a clear one. I mean, given the way that the contract was managed, as I said, I
would - my speculation would be it was with Jason McNamara.
COMMISSIONER: Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you, Commissioner. Would you agree, though, that the visual
presentation - and we will come to it - doesn't descend into the level of detail of the latest
version of the draft of the report?

MR GREGGERY: That is, it contains much more information about PwC's analysis of the
design of the system, the suitability of the data to the system, the scope for improvement of
the system, the expectation about whether Budget Measures might be achieved or not.
There are a range of topics about which a very high level of detail is provided in the latest
version of the draft report.
MR WEST: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Logically, that level of analysis undertaken by PwC, for which it quoted on
that understanding that it would be required to do that level of analysis, was a level of
analysis which would be of real assistance to the Department, from your perspective, in the
way it assessed and redesigned the Scheme if necessary.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Were you concerned, then, when you came to realise that the Department
wasn't interested in that level of detail, that they were paying PwC for not giving them
something that might be helpful?
MR WEST: So my recollection is of the time - we are talking about, so kind of May, June of
2017 - was -
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR WEST: Focus of the Department at the time had kind of shifted to implementing changes
rather than, you know, a more detailed understanding about perhaps what was - what led to
the need for those changes to be implemented.
MR GREGGERY: But there's a logical difficulty with that, isn't there? It's a bit hard to make
some changes without understanding what leads to the need for those changes, and a lot of
those - that information was in the draft report.
MR WEST: As I say, my recollection is that - if you take that presentation paper, that
suggested a range of strategies that the Department had accepted that they were good
things to do, and attention turned to implementing them.
MR GREGGERY: I appreciate that, but PwC is in possession of its detailed analysis of the
Scheme in all of its areas. Why wasn't it provided anyway? I mean, you've done the work. It
informs the Department.
MR WEST: I think the only explanation that I've got for that is it wasn't completed. Like, it
wasn't completed to a point at which we would have been comfortable providing it to the
client. And we subsequently were advised that it - that the presentation formed the report
and so we didn't seek to do the additional work to finalise a report that wasn't required
under the contract.

MR GREGGERY: Were you concerned, then, the Department really wasn't interested in the
level of analysis that PwC had undertaken? And just didn't want to know?
MR WEST: No, I didn't - I didn't get that concern.
COMMISSIONER: Did you tell anybody at the Department that you had this useful analysis,
which was not really quite complete, but it was there if they wanted it?
MR WEST: So, I don't - I don't recall ever telling them that we had it in a physical copy, but,
you know, during the course of the engagement, a number of the conversations through that
engagement would have led us to the drafting what was in that draft. So -
COMMISSIONER: Yes, but what I'm asking you is, did you intimate to anybody in the
Department that PwC had got this report which was not finalised, but a lot of work had gone
into, if they wanted it?
MR WEST: No, I don't recall ever doing that.
COMMISSIONER: Because it would have given them the option?
MR WEST: Yes, it would have also required - it wasn't completed to a point at which we
would have been comfortable providing it to the client.
COMMISSIONER: You said that, but you didn't even tell them that this thing existed in any
form, from what you were saying?
MR WEST: Yes, not that I can recall and not that we were able to find in responding to the
request for information.
COMMISSIONER: Nobody in the Department indicated to you they would rather not have it?
MR WEST: No. I don't - like I - I don't recall ever having anyone from PwC ever indicating to
the Department that it existed.
MR GREGGERY: Well, Mr West, I will take you to Exhibit 3903. I think it's tab 92 in your
bundle. Sorry, 3900 now. I think there has been some renumbering since last Friday, which
might continue to catch me out. The email is from Frank Van Hagen. Was he within PwC?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: He was involved in the project?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Involved in developing the draft report?

MR GREGGERY: To you and others within PwC?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And were those others involved in developing the draft report?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Were you involved in developing the draft report?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Okay. By 4 May 2017, there is the latest draft, which you would agree
indicates earlier versions of it which had been developed throughout PwC's analysis since
February?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And you were asked to decide whether you were comfortable with the
current version and, if you were, that it would be good to share it with Jason McNamara to
give them an idea of the scope of the report and its recommendations, of course with the
caveat that it was a working draft. Firstly, were you comfortable with that version of the
report? In terms of the analysis PwC had undertaken to that point in time?
MR WEST: So, my recollection is I wouldn't have been comfortable with that - with providing
that version of the report to anybody outside of PwC.
MR GREGGERY: Why is that?
MR WEST: Because I don't think it had been completed and it hadn't gone through an
internal quality assurance process.
MR GREGGERY: But with the caveat that it was a working a draft as opposed to a completed
version that had gone through quality assurance process, and that it was provided in hard
copy, which was what proposed, that wouldn't have presented any problems for PwC, would
it?
MR WEST: Yes, yes, it would have still presented a problem for me.
MR GREGGERY: What problems are there?
MR WEST: The major problem is that when you give somebody a - an unfinished or a draft
version of something it - some things in that have a habit of sticking in people's mind even if
they are subsequently removed or are incorrect in the - in the final report.

MR WEST: I think so, yes.
COMMISSIONER: So do you never in your dealings with government Departments provide a
draft report because of those issues?
MR WEST: We sometimes provide drafts before finalising, but I - not incomplete drafts.
MR GREGGERY: If we go then to -
COMMISSIONER: Sorry, I'm just trying to understand that. Didn't you just say this was the
final version of the draft?
MR WEST: This was the point at which we stopped working on the report.
COMMISSIONER: I see in that sense, okay. And what made you stop at that point?
MR WEST: I'm not sure if it was exactly that day, but it was - that would be - that must have
been the - around the period that it became clear that the previously mentioned document
was considered to constitute a report for the purpose of the work order.
COMMISSIONER: Were you able to tell us how that was made clear?
MR WEST: As I say, I can't recall, but my speculation would be through conversations with
the Department.
MR GREGGERY: The attachment to the email indicates, I think, the date of 4 May 2017, DHS
Integrity Modernisation Implementation Strategy draft version 0.25. What's the significance
of 0.25?
MR WEST: So, without knowing for sure, that would have been a numbering convention on
drafting. So there were - would have been previous drafts that had numbers less than 0.25.
But I'm not sure if it went sequentially from 0.1 to 0.25. Ostensibly a version control.
MR GREGGERY: Does a version that indicates 1.0 and 1.25 indicate that it's been reviewed by
someone at a higher level at PwC?
MR WEST: No, not necessarily.
MR GREGGERY: To your knowledge, it's just a sequential numbering system, but it might not
be every number in the sequence?
MR WEST: Yes, that's right, and there's no specific number that indicates a particular step
has taken place.
MR GREGGERY: To be clear, DHS Integrity Modernisation Implementation Strategy was the

MR WEST: Yes, I think so. I would need to confirm, by looking at that attachment.
MR GREGGERY: I might do that briefly. 3901. I think this is right. Tab 61, I think, in your
bundle.
COMMISSIONER: Is it, Mr West? It's not in mine -
MR WEST: No, it's not in mine.
MR GREGGERY: Well, in your preparation before giving evidence, Mr West, do you now recall
that version of the draft?
MR WEST: Yes, I recall providing versions of the draft. It's a bit hard to tell from the -
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR WEST: - cover page alone whether or not that's the -
MR GREGGERY: Alright.
MR WEST: I've got no reason to think what was attached to the email wasn't.
MR GREGGERY: That's okay. That copy of the draft in my bundle is 71 pages long.
COMMISSIONER: It's at 89, I think.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you, Commissioner. I might just flick through it.
MR WEST: Yes, so I think there is a - somewhere there is a more recent version than what is
at tab 89.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, alright.
MR WEST: Because I think - the only reason I say that is I think there is a version that has
some wording in the Executive Summary, but that one doesn't.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. If we go to page .4119, you can see that the Executive Summary is yet to
be inserted. That's what you are pointing to on the hard copy?
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And can you confirm with me that, otherwise, the report run, including all
annexures and miscellaneous items, for 71 or 72 pages?
MR WEST: Yes, that's right.

MR GREGGERY: Yes. It looks like it's at a relatively advanced stage of development on its
face.
MR WEST: Yes, yes.
MR GREGGERY: So if we move to Exhibit 4774, this is an email from Mr Bowe. He was a
senior manager in PwC working on the project?
MR WEST: Yes, that's right.
MR GREGGERY: And it's an email to Mr Weber and to yourself, which attaches a draft which
appears to bear the date 30 May 2017. That is the date of the email.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: It's version 1.0.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Now there, are two copies of it attached. One is smaller than the other in
terms of megabytes. Sorry, one is Word, and one is PDF. Thank you.
MR WEST: Yes, I think that's just the difference.
MR GREGGERY: And it refers to a discussion a couple of weeks ago with DHS that the draft
report would be provided around 2 June and DHS intended that it be marked
protected/sensitive Cabinet. Does that prompt your memory of the timing up to which the
drafts were developed?
MR WEST: Yes, I mean, that tells me that we were still working on the draft at the end of
May.
MR GREGGERY: At the end of May. And that there was an anticipation from a couple of
weeks earlier that document would be provided within a couple of days of this email? That is
by 2 June?
MR WEST: Yes, that a document will be provided around 2 June.
MR GREGGERY: Well, the document is the draft report.
MR WEST: So, like I say, I don't recall ever having a conversation with the Department about
the provision of the attachment to that email, as a draft report.
MR GREGGERY: You may not, but Mr Bowe clearly indicates there was one. That's what this
email records, isn't it, Mr West?

MR WEST: So that email records that there would be the provision of a DHS Implementation
Strategy document.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Which is the document which is attached to this email. You can see that
from the second paragraph?
MR WEST: Which turned out to be the presentation that we spoke about previously.
MR GREGGERY: Well, that might not be right, Mr West. What this email makes clear, I
suggest, is that the document which is attached to it is the DHS Integrity Modernisation
Implementation Strategy, which is described in short form in the first sentence as the DHS
Implementation Strategy document. And in the second paragraph, it confirms that what is
attached is the latest version of what is described in short form as the DHS Implementation
Strategy document which is, in fact, the draft report as it's described fully in the title. It's
clearly what it communicates.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And what was attached was a draft report as at 30 May 2017.
MR WEST: Yes, so what was attached was still clearly at that point in time our understanding
of what we were - would subsequently be providing to the Department.
MR GREGGERY: And by subsequently, you mean later that week?
MR WEST: Yes, or some point post that date, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Well, 2 June, around the 2nd of June.
MR WEST: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Right. And by this point in time, PwC had already given a presentation to
